da-non-sequitur.evidence: nucleon-ordering-factorization.md:104-110 the proton–neutron crossing matrix T_pn uses d=−½(q−q⁻¹) justified by 'T_pn = ½(σ0+σ0⁻¹)' (md:156). Averaging the over- and under-crossing operators to model a p–n crossing is asserted, not derived from a topological rule.
da-non-sequitur.notes: The ½(σ0+σ0⁻¹) prescription for mixed nucleon crossings is a modeling choice presented as a 'crossing convention'; the step from 'p–n pair' to 'symmetric average of the two crossings' has no cited lemma. The pp/nn cases (σ0 / σ0⁻¹) are natural; the mixed case is the gap.

da-referee-verdict.notes: verdict: minor-revision. referee_argument: The factorization is structurally credible and its easy half (scalar-channel ordering independence) is Lean-proved sorry-free. But the block is presented as a proved 'Proposition' while its central master identity (the Wedderburn channel decomposition) is discharged by sorry in the matching Lean decl — Lean proves strictly less than the .md claims (da-lean-narrative-divergence, major). Secondary: the mixed p–n crossing matrix uses an undeclared symmetric-average prescription ½(σ0+σ0⁻¹) (da-non-sequitur). Recommend either (a) restate the master half as conditional/conjectural pending the Hecke engine, or (b) land the Wedderburn-decomposition lemma.
